summary: I developed ZERO-G IGNITION, an interactive web dashboard and 3D volumetric combustion simulator designed to study about fire safety under microgravity (0G) and Earth (1G) environments. To address deep-space habitat fire risks—such as Artemis lunar bases operating with elevated oxygen concentrations—my platform integrate real NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigation data, including BASS-II, E-FIELD, and CFI-G. Powered by a custom GLSL raymarching shader engine, it accurately simulates complex microgravity combustion phenomena like spherical flame propagation and high-voltage ion-wind suppression. This project is vital because standard Earth-based firefighting models fail in space due to the absence of buoyant convection. ZERO-G IGNITION provides researchers and engineers an essential pre-mission risk assessment tool, featuring live telemetry and professional CSV data export to safeguard human space exploration.
details:
ZERO-G IGNITION is an interactive 3D web dashboard and multi-physics combustion simulator that I developed to analyze fire behavior in microgravity (0G) compared to Earth gravity (1G). It works by integrating real experimental datasets from NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI)—such as BASS-II, E-FIELD, and CFI-G—into a real-time dual-chamber 3D viewport. Users can adjust environmental variables like oxygen concentration, fuel flux, and duct airflow to observe spherical flame propagation, aerosol coagulation, and high-voltage ion-wind suppression.

The main benefit of my project is providing an accessible, physics-backed pre-mission risk assessment tool without needing expensive physical tests on the ISS. Its intended impact is to improve habitat fire safety for future Artemis lunar bases and deep-space missions, while also inspiring terrestrial spin-offs like advanced smoke detectors.

To build this platform, I used HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js, and custom GLSL volumetric raymarching shaders. My project is creative because it replaces heavy pre-rendered animations with live mathematical rendering of buoyant convection and thermal fields, alongside live telemetry graphs and instant CSV data export. During development, I carefully considered about how elevated oxygen levels and reduced ambient pressure in space habitats change ignition thresholds and soot accumulation, ensuring that the simulation reflect real NASA experimental findings accurately. This tool provide researchers and students a clear way to visualize complex space fire physics.
